newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai aims to increase 97 exports to $14 bln.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai aims to increase 97 exports to $14 bln.

text.p: The city of Shanghai, China's economic hub, aims to increase exports to $14 billion in 1997, from $13.2 billion in 1996, China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.

Shanghai's 1996 exports, which rose 14 percent compared with the year earlier figure, accounted for more than eight percent of China's total, the newspaper quoted Zhu Xiaoming, the director of Shanghai's foreign economic relations and trade commission, as saying.
Shanghai's government planned to authorise about five overseas-invested, joint-venture foreign trade companies, the first of their kind in China, the newspaper said.
Shanghai and the southern boomtown of Shenzhen have been chosen as the sites for joint-venture foreign trade firms, with regulations issued last year, it said.
Zhu said the step could bring in advanced management and trade channels and help boost exports.

Overseas-invested companies in Shanghai would probably increase their exports by 20 percent in 1997, Zhu said. In 1996, these enterprises exported $4 billion worth of products, almost twice the value of the previous year, he said.
